abstract: Interpreting gene lists and expression data from Caenorhabditis elegans experiments usually means writing scripts, searching scattered databases or uploading unpublished data to a remote server. WormIE (Worm Integrated Explorer, https://wormie.bio) is a free, open-source tool for analyzing user-provided data and exploring C. elegans annotations in one browser tab. Starting with gene lists from -omics experiments, genetic screens or other approaches, users can explore what genes have in common and how they interact, test over-representation or ranked-list enrichment in built-in or user-provided gene sets and compare lists by their genes or enriched categories. Of WormIE's nine collections, which include Gene Ontology and CeNGEN neuron types, two are curated sets found in no other worm resource: neuronal genes and synaptic genes. WormIE counts aligned reads from RNA sequencing and tests for differential expression with the same R package as conventional pipelines, then checks the genes for enrichment in those collections. Clicking any gene in a result page opens the gene page gathering seventeen domains from WormBase, the Alliance of Genome Resources and other sources, such as phenotypes, interactions and expression. Everything runs on the user's computer without uploading data and works offline. On simulated data, every analysis agreed with its R counterpart (correlation 0.9999), and in a reanalysis of a germline study of the co-regulator SIN-3, WormIE recovered 99% of the reported differentially expressed genes and all nine WormCat categories. Together, these results show that WormIE reliably links gene lists and expression data to community-curated knowledge without programming or a server.
